book_meta.work: short stories by Guy de Maupassant and Anton Chekhov
book_meta.author: Maupassant (d. 1893) and Chekhov (d. 1904)
book_meta.status: public domain — retold from the plots, no translation used

sentences.ar: السيدة أوريل كانت مرا بتحسب كل قرش، بس مش عشان هي فقيرة.
sentences.en: Madame Oreille was a woman who counted every penny, but not because she was poor.

sentences.ar: كانت بتحسب لأنه الصرف بيوجعها، زي الجرح.
sentences.en: She counted because spending pained her, like a wound.

sentences.ar: وزوجها، موظف بالوزارة، راتبه محدود، وعمره ما شاف منه قرش.
sentences.en: And her husband, a clerk at the ministry, had a limited salary, and never saw a penny of it.

sentences.ar: وكان كل صبح يروح عالشغل بشمسية مقطعة، وزملاؤه بيضحكوا.
sentences.en: And every morning he went to work with a torn umbrella, and his colleagues laughed.

sentences.ar: وبيوم انفجر، وقال: بدي شمسية جديدة!
sentences.en: And one day he exploded, and said: I want a new umbrella!
Or I leave the house!

sentences.ar: وبعد أسبوع من النقاش، اشترت له وحدة بتمانية فرنكات.
sentences.en: And after a week of argument, she bought him one for eight francs.

sentences.ar: وقالت: هاي بتخدمك خمس سنين على الأقل.
sentences.en: And said: this will serve you five years at least.

sentences.ar: وبعد شهر، رجع الزوج، والشمسية فيها ثقب زغير محروق.
sentences.en: And a month later, the husband came home, and the umbrella had a small burnt hole.
The wife screamed: what is this?
He said: I do not know!
I found it like that!
She said: liar!
You burned it with your cigar!

sentences.ar: وقعدت طول الليل تبكي على التمانية فرنكات.
sentences.en: And she sat all night crying over the eight francs.

sentences.ar: وتاني يوم، رجع الزوج، والشمسية كلها ثقوب محروقة.
sentences.en: And the next day, the husband came home, and the umbrella was all burnt holes.
Ten, twenty, row after row.
He said: my colleagues.
They did it on purpose, to laugh at me.

sentences.ar: وهالمرة صدقته، لأنه ما حدا بيحرق شمسيته عشرين مرة بالغلط.
sentences.en: And this time she believed him, because no one burns his own umbrella twenty times by accident.
And she sat thinking, the tears on her cheeks.

sentences.ar: وبعدين تذكرت: البيت مؤمن ضد الحريق.
sentences.en: And then she remembered: the house was insured against fire.
And the umbrella was in the house.

sentences.ar: ولبست أحسن فستان، وراحت لشركة التأمين، وطلبت المدير.
sentences.en: And she put on her best dress, went to the insurance company, and asked for the director.

sentences.ar: وقالت، بصوت المصيبة: صار عنا حريق.
sentences.en: And said, in a voice of catastrophe: we have had a fire.
The director stood, and said: a fire!
Where?
How?
What is the loss?
She said: an umbrella.
He said: what?

sentences.ar: قالت: شمسية حرير، بتمانية فرنكات، احترقت.
sentences.en: She said: a silk umbrella, eight francs, burnt.
And put the umbrella on the table.

sentences.ar: المدير تطلع بالشمسية، وبالمرا، وصار يفهم شوي شوي.
sentences.en: The director looked at the umbrella, and at the woman, and began to understand, little by little.

sentences.ar: قال: يا سيدتي، التأمين ضد الحريق للبيوت.
sentences.en: He said: madame, fire insurance is for houses.
Not for umbrellas.
She said: and the umbrella was in the house!
And the house is insured!
Where does it say umbrellas are excluded?

sentences.ar: وحكت القصة كلها، من البداية، بالتفصيل، والدمع بعينها.
sentences.en: And she told the whole story, from the beginning, in detail, tears in her eyes.
And told it again.

sentences.ar: وبعد نص ساعة، المدير قال: طيب.
sentences.en: And after half an hour, the director said: fine.
Fine.

sentences.ar: خدي الشمسية لمحل، وصلحيها، وابعتي لنا الفاتورة.
sentences.en: Take the umbrella to a shop, have it repaired, and send us the bill.
And she left pleased, her head high.

sentences.ar: وراحت لأغلى محل بباريس، وقالت: بدي حرير.
sentences.en: And she went to the most expensive shop in Paris, and said: I want silk.
The best silk.
The price does not matter.
The company pays.
